injections.rationale: Wrong-but-plausible formula. The Dirac monopole charge in Gaussian units is g₀ = e/(2α) where α is the fine-structure constant (so g/e = 1/(2α) ≈ 68.5, giving g ≈ 3.3×10^-8 esu). Replacing with g = 2eα flips the relationship: the injected formula gives g ≈ 7×10^-12 esu (4 orders of magnitude smaller than the stated value 3.3×10^-8). Wolfram refutes by symbolic comparison against the canonical Dirac quantization e·g = ℏc/2 (Gaussian) → g = ℏc/(2e) = e/(2α).
injections.ground_truth_description: Replaced the canonical Dirac monopole charge formula 'g = e/(2α)' with the structurally similar but algebraically wrong 'g = 2eα'. The numerical value '3.3×10^-8 esu' (correct for the original formula) is preserved, creating an internal inconsistency between formula and value.
